title: Maximum Partition Factor
summary: Given a 2D integer array points, where points[i] = [xi, yi] are coordinates on the Cartesian plane, find the maximum partition factor by splitting the points into exactly two non-empty groups.
statement: Given a 2D integer array points, where points[i] = [xi, yi] are coordinates on the Cartesian plane, find the maximum partition factor by splitting the points into exactly two non-empty groups. The partition factor is the minimum Manhattan distance between any two points in the same group. Return the highest possible partition factor for any valid split. For n=2, define the partition factor as 0 since there are no intra-group pairs.
constraints: Two to 500 Cartesian points may contain negative coordinates or duplicates.
Split all points into exactly two nonempty groups.
The factor is the minimum Manhattan distance between points in the same group; a two-point input has factor zero.
hints: For a proposed factor d, every pair closer than d must be placed in opposite groups.
Those required separations form a graph; the factor is feasible exactly when that graph is bipartite.
Binary-search the distinct Manhattan distances and test each conflict graph by two-coloring.
A valid coloring produces the split, while an odd conflict cycle proves no two groups can separate every too-close pair.
editorial: A valid coloring produces the split, while an odd conflict cycle proves no two groups can separate every too-close pair.

tests.explanation: Coloring opposite corners together gives within-group distance four.
Putting the first point alone leaves the other pair at Manhattan distance eleven.
